topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text: The bear was soft, too soft, like the clouds that sometimes whisper too close. The yard was a place of old whispers, where shadows danced on the edges of laughter. I found him, there, under the sun that cast too long a shadow. His eyes, those button eyes, they watched the world pass with a silence that echoed through the years. I picked him up, and the world tilted, just a little. The air grew thick, heavy with the scent of yesterdays that shouldn’t be revisited. The bear was cold, colder than I remember, and I couldn’t hold onto him for too long. I left him there, under the watchful eyes of others, hoping he wouldn’t remember me, hoping I wouldn’t remember him.
